A1.justification: Both complete, 22-page PDFs describe DARS and support reliable comparison of text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B. Renamed and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original scoring experiments on six datasets, human evaluation of reflections, scaling experiments, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Table 1, human evaluation, scaling and ablation figures, and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Both versions synthesize reflections from thought-tree path differences, separately train the Reasoner and Critic, and refine assessments until the Critic outputs STOP. v2 explicitly distinguishes SFT training from inference-time interaction, clarifying the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both use ASAP 1, 2, 5, and 6 plus the same two private biology datasets, renamed proprietary in v2. The unseen-question evaluation is retained. The newly stated subset exclusions explain existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the DeBERTa-v3-large classifier, SFT, DPO, and GPT-4-turbo Critic comparisons. Appendix comparison methods also remain. GPT-4 as Critic is a renamed comparator.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, ACC/macro-F1/QWK metrics, training settings, model sizes, decoding procedures, and human-evaluation sampling remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same settings and 20 sampled instances per dataset.

E4.justification: The scaling, weak-Reasoner, refinement-data, single-model, unseen-question, and architecture analyses are retained. Appendix B preserves the DPO regularization analysis, error analysis, and five case studies. The separate human-evaluation subsection reorganizes existing material.

E5.justification: Both retain five classifier runs with the same listed seeds, three runs for generative baselines and non-scaling DARS experiments, and the same one-tailed t-test and significance notation.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative results are retained. Table 1's overall DARS ACC/F1/QWK remain 0.7247/0.6437/0.8113. The new Figure 1 bars summarize results already shown in Figure 4; revised Figures 4 and 10 preserve their outcomes.

T1.justification: The scoring function, binary path encoding, difference vector, reflection-generation equations, and iterative recurrence remain mathematically equivalent. Notation changes and the expanded graph-based explanation introduce no new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract refocuses the work on ASAS and broadens its performance claim from preference-optimization methods to existing ASAS baselines. This broader comparison is unsupported by the unchanged Table 1, where the classifier retains higher overall scores. The central contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a sequential-decoding versus graph-structured reasoning explanation, discusses possible rule-based extensions to mathematics and code, and acknowledges that prompts were not exhaustively optimized. Existing empirical interpretations and appendix failure analyses remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises future release of training data and code; v2 provides a code-release link. Appendix A newly discloses the proprietary data's provenance, anonymization, and non-sharing restriction. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting graph-based reasoning and recent assessment work, including LeCun, Subramaniam, DRIFT, and LearnLens, while removing several preference-optimization and reward-modeling references. The principal related-work comparisons remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, human evaluation becomes a separate subsection, and terminology and explanatory structure are revised throughout the main text.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 rearrange and redraw existing illustrations, with an added summary chart in Figure 1. Figure 4 changes completion-rate axis formatting, Figure 10 changes sizing, and captions and appendix placements change. Most result figures and table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies the previously confusing training/inference distinction, improves the method narrative, supplies code-access information, and states additional limitations. These provide a modest gain in clarity and reproducibility while the empirical evidence remains unchanged. The gain is qualified by the abstract's broader claim of outperforming ASAS baselines, which Table 1 does not support.
